name: Actinium
occurrence: Extremely rare, found in trace amounts within uranium ores as a decay product.
majorUses: Lends its name to the entire actinide series
safetyNotes: Highly radioactive, requiring specialized shielding and handling even in the tiny quantities used in research.
notableCharacteristics: Glows faintly with a pale blue light in the dark, similar to radium, because of its intense radioactivity — the origin of its name from the Greek 'aktinos', meaning 'ray' or 'beam'.
whyHere: As the element that gives the entire actinide series its name, actinium's single 6d electron marks the analogous starting point to lanthanum at the top of the f-block's second row, even though — like lanthanum — it isn't itself filling an f-orbital.
didYouKnow: A gram of actinium glows visibly in the dark purely from its own radioactivity, releasing enough energy to excite the surrounding air, similar to (though even more intensely than) radium.
genZNote: Gives its name to the whole actinide series while also glowing blue in the dark. Extra, but earned it.
